stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under key ML/AI tags including 'transformers' and 'llama'.
The pipeline indicates its primary use case is 'text-generation'.

stories.title: It's official: EU will force Google to share search data and open up AI on Android
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: The EU is mandating that Google share search data and open up its AI capabilities on Android.
This regulatory action represents a significant shift in how major tech platforms operate within the EU.
Google has publicly stated that these required changes pose potential risks to user privacy and security.

stories.title: RoboTTT: Context Scaling for Robot Policies
stories.author: Linxi "Jim" Fan
bullet_points: Introduces RoboTTT, a method to scale visuomotor context for robot policies up to 8K timesteps.
Achieves this massive context scaling without increasing inference latency, a significant technical feat.
Enables new capabilities such as one-shot in-context imitation and on-the-fly policy improvement in robots.

stories.title: RoboTTT: Context Scaling for Robot Policies
stories.author: Linxi "Jim" Fan
bullet_points: Introduces RoboTTT, a method to scale visuomotor context for robot policies up to 8K timesteps.
Achieves this massive context scaling without increasing inference latency, a significant technical hurdle.
Unlocks new capabilities, including one-shot in-context imitation and on-the-fly policy improvement.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized for text-generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It points to the use of standard NLP pipelines, specifically text-generation.
The model is categorized under key ML technologies like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Highlights the trending status of the DeepSeek-V4-Pro model on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a substantial developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.31 introduces significant speed improvements for Gemma 4 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Speedup reaches up to 90% when running with coding agents, as validated by the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher quality outputs, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The key feature is that these agents can run entirely on the user's local hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, facilitating local LLM execution.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for enhanced performance.
The integration specifically targets Apple Silicon, optimizing AI workloads on Apple hardware.
This feature is currently available in preview, indicating an ongoing optimization effort for local AI.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a new personal AI assistant designed for local execution.
It integrates messaging applications with local AI coding agents.
The core feature emphasizes running all AI processes entirely on the user's own device for privacy/control.

stories.title: Google is better than Apple at playing the AI regulations game
stories.author: Robert Hart
bullet_points: The EU has mandated that Google grant greater access to Android for its AI competitors.
This regulatory action forces Google to open up its Android ecosystem, despite past resistance.
The story frames this as a regulatory shift impacting the competitive landscape of AI development.

stories.title: Roblox will let people use AI to make games on their phone
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Roblox is integrating AI tools directly into its mobile application for game creation.
This move signals Roblox's significant embrace of generative AI technology within its platform.
The feature raises concerns about potential content overload and quality control on the platform.

stories.title: SpaceX scrubs Starship launch after some of its engines didn't start
stories.author: Stephen Clark
bullet_points: SpaceX has postponed the Starship launch attempt.
The delay was caused by failures in some of the vehicle's engines failing to ignite.
The company plans to conduct propellant offloading before the next attempt, which is anticipated in a few days.

stories.title: Fear of humanoid robots spurs human workers to strike at Hyundai auto factory
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: Hyundai plans to deploy 25,000 Atlas humanoid robots in its US factories starting in 2028.
The deployment signals a major industrial shift toward advanced robotics in manufacturing.
Worker fear regarding job displacement is leading to strikes at the Hyundai auto factory.

stories.title: Now, even Russia's most elite hackers are using Clickfix to infect devices
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: Clickfix, a social-engineering technique, is now being utilized by highly sophisticated actors, including elite Russian hackers.
The technique has historically been associated primarily with financially motivated cybercriminals.
The adoption by state-level or elite hacking groups indicates a potential escalation in the threat landscape.

stories.title: Pretraining Data Can Be Poisoned through Computational Propaganda
stories.author: Kyle Lo
bullet_points: The research demonstrates that pretraining data for Large Language Models (LLMs) can be poisoned to introduce harmful behaviors.
Unlike prior work, this study shows poisoning attacks are feasible beyond limited sources like Wikipedia, targeting large-scale, heterogeneous corpora.
The attack specifically addresses the interaction between poisoned data and existing data curation pipelines, highlighting a critical vulnerability.

stories.title: SceneBind: Binding What and Where Across Vision, Audio and Language
stories.author: Eli Shlizerman
bullet_points: SceneBind introduces an omni-modal representation that integrates vision, audio, and language for scene understanding.
It addresses a key limitation in current models by explicitly incorporating 3D spatial structure, moving beyond mere instance-level semantics.
The core innovation is representing scenes as semantic-spatial entities using a combination of global and object-centric embeddings.

stories.title: AutoSynthesis: An agentic system for automated meta-analysis
stories.author: Stefan Feuerriegel
bullet_points: Introduces AutoSynthesis, an end-to-end multi-agent system designed for automated meta-analysis.
Addresses the current bottleneck in evidence synthesis, which is largely manual and difficult to scale.
The system takes a natural language research question and automates the entire process from search strategy formulation to data extraction.

stories.title: When Words Are Safe But Actions Kill: Probing Physical Danger Beyond Text Safety in Hidden-State Risk Space
stories.author: Ke Xu
bullet_points: Investigates the critical gap where linguistically safe LLM instructions become physically dangerous when controlling embodied agents.
Demonstrates that physical danger (PD) and traditional text content danger (CD) are distinct, separable signals within LLM representations.
Uses advanced techniques like hidden-state direction analysis to probe safety risks in LLMs (specifically tested on Qwen2.5 models).

stories.title: Pretraining Data Can Be Poisoned through Computational Propaganda
stories.author: Kyle Lo
bullet_points: The research demonstrates that Large Language Models (LLMs) can be poisoned during pretraining using computational propaganda.
Previous poisoning research was limited to established sources like Wikipedia, failing to account for large-scale, heterogeneous pretraining corpora.
The study highlights the difficulty in detecting and mitigating harmful behaviors introduced by these advanced data poisoning attacks.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces improved performance and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware configurations.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, specifically improving capabilities on Apple silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra.
The model is specifically designed for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is optimized for supporting long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for advanced AI features within Claude Code.
The new capabilities include the implementation of 'subagents' for more complex task decomposition.
Web search functionality has been added to enhance Claude Code's ability to access real-time information.

stories.title: Fortnite is getting a bunch of AI-powered ‘personas’
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Epic Games is integrating AI-powered 'personas' into Fortnite experiences.
Creators will be able to publish experiences featuring AI characters with consistent voices starting July 30th.
Thirty-six pre-made AI characters, including Fortnite staples, are available for creators to use as NPCs.

stories.title: Netflix says around 300 titles used generative AI
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Netflix reported that approximately 300 titles on its platform utilized generative AI.
The majority of the AI application was noted to be in the post-production phase of content creation.
Netflix cited the use of generative AI to achieve higher quality output faster and at a reduced cost.

stories.title: Google is renaming NotebookLM to Gemini Notebook
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Google is rebranding its AI note-taking application from NotebookLM to Gemini Notebook.
The app will continue to function as a standalone product while increasing integration with Gemini and Google Search.
The renaming signals a deeper alignment of the product with Google's broader Gemini AI ecosystem.

stories.title: HP fined 1.4 billion rupees for “cartelization” of ink cartridges, toner, PCs
stories.author: Scharon Harding
bullet_points: HP was fined 1.4 billion rupees for alleged 'cartelization' practices related to its printing supplies.
The regulatory action stems from threats by resellers to switch to counterfeit ink cartridges and toners.
The case involves the alleged monopolistic control over PC and printing supply markets by HP.

stories.title: xAI can’t deny Grok makes CSAM anymore. So it’s suing users.
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: xAI has filed a lawsuit against a Grok user accused of creating child sexual abuse material (CSAM).
This marks the first reported lawsuit by xAI concerning misuse of the Grok AI.
The incident highlights ongoing challenges regarding AI safety, content moderation, and illegal content generation.

stories.title: SciDiagramEdit: Learning to Edit Scientific Diagrams from Paper Revisions
stories.author: Jürgen Schmidhuber
bullet_points: SciDiagramEdit addresses the manual and time-consuming process of editing scientific figures during paper revisions.
The system aims to automate figure editing using natural language instructions.
The challenge lies in the complex, heterogeneous visual grammar of scientific diagrams (schematics, plots, arrows, etc.).

stories.title: Beyond Success Rate: Cost-Aware Evaluation of Offensive and Defensive Security Agents
stories.author: Yaron Singer
bullet_points: The paper introduces a novel evaluation metric for AI security agents that incorporates operational cost alongside success rate.
Current security agent evaluations often overlook the resource consumption (inference budget) of individual reasoning steps and tool calls.
The research tests this cost-aware evaluation on offensive (Cybench) and defensive (Splunk BOTS v1) security challenges.

stories.title: SearchOS-V1: Towards Robust Open-Domain Information-Seeking Agent Collaboration
stories.author: Zhicheng Dou
bullet_points: Introduces SearchOS, a system-level multi-agent framework designed to improve information-seeking.
Addresses a key limitation in current LLM agents: struggling to track task progress and getting stuck in repetitive search loops.
Focuses on enhancing the robustness and efficiency of open-domain information retrieval by managing complex interaction histories.

stories.title: teLLMe Why (Ain't Nothing but a Jam): Exploratory Causal Analysis of Urban Driving Data
stories.author: Jorge Ortiz
bullet_points: Introduces 'teLLMe,' a system designed for exploratory causal analysis of urban driving datasets.
Addresses the challenge of answering causal questions (e.g., 'How would rain change traffic density?') using purely observational traffic data.
Combines causal structure learning with structured event tables derived from dashcam annotations to enable deeper insights.

stories.title: In-Place Tokenizer Expansion for Pre-trained LLMs
stories.author: Mathias Lechner
bullet_points: Current LLM tokenizers are fixed based on pre-training priorities, leading to inefficiencies for later-added languages.
Adding new languages can result in increased tokenization overhead (more tokens per word), raising latency and compute costs.
The impact of this tokenization inefficiency is more pronounced on compact models compared to large cloud models.

stories.title: Online Neural Space Time Memory for Dynamic Novel View Synthesis
stories.author: Xuan Luo
bullet_points: Addresses the real-time constraint challenge in dynamic novel view synthesis from streaming video.
Identifies the computational bottleneck of standard Test-Time Training (TTT) due to required gradient-based memory updates.
Proposes an 'Online Neural Space Time Memory' to overcome the trade-off between long-horizon memory and real-time performance.

stories.title: Mutable Low-Rank Sketches for Retrain-Free Recommendation
stories.author: Nick Clayton
bullet_points: Addresses the 'embedding staleness' bottleneck in two-stage recommendation systems.
Introduces 'mutable sketches' using a KP-tree structure to store user preferences.
Allows for on-the-fly embedding recomputation as new ratings arrive, improving prediction accuracy.

stories.title: In-Place Tokenizer Expansion for Pre-trained LLMs
stories.author: Mathias Lechner
bullet_points: Current LLM tokenizers are fixed based on initial training corpus priorities, leading to suboptimal performance for later-added languages.
Adding new languages can result in increased tokenization overhead (more tokens per word), negatively impacting latency, compute, and energy use.
The paper proposes an 'In-Place Tokenizer Expansion' method to address this inefficiency, particularly relevant for resource-constrained (compact) models.

stories.title: NeuronSoup: Evolving Asynchronous, Shared-Neuron Temporal Graphs without Backpropagation
stories.author: Subodh Kalia
bullet_points: Introduces NeuronSoup, a novel neural computation architecture moving away from traditional synchronous processing.
Employs asynchronous, delay-mediated signal propagation through a pool of shared neurons.
Proposes a mechanism for continuous-valued signal routing through shared hidden neurons, bypassing backpropagation.

stories.title: BadWAM: When World-Action Models Dream Right but Act Wrong
stories.author: Xinchao Wang
bullet_points: World-Action Models (WAMs) are a new paradigm for embodied control, coupling action generation with future world prediction.
The paper introduces 'BadWAM' to challenge the assumption that this coupling inherently leads to robustness and safety.
BadWAM provides a unified framework for modeling and evaluating the potential failures in these advanced control systems.

stories.title: SciDiagramEdit: Learning to Edit Scientific Diagrams from Paper Revisions
stories.author: Jürgen Schmidhuber
bullet_points: SciDiagramEdit addresses the challenging task of automating scientific diagram editing based on natural language instructions.
The system aims to handle complex scientific figures composed of heterogeneous elements like schematics, plots, and arrows.
This research targets a routine but time-consuming bottleneck in the academic research and manuscript revision workflow.

stories.title: Bridge Evidence: Static Retrieval Utility Does Not Predict Causal Utility in Multi-Step Agentic Search
stories.author: Shubham Chatterjee
bullet_points: Traditional retrieval evaluation (static usefulness) fails when language models operate as multi-step search agents.
The utility of a retrieved document depends not just on its content relative to the current query, but on what it enables the agent to do next.
The research highlights a gap between static document relevance and dynamic, causal utility in agentic workflows.

stories.title: Beyond the Leaderboard: Design Lessons for Trustworthy Multimodal VQA
stories.author: Steven A. Hicks
bullet_points: The research focuses on designing trustworthy and interpretable multimodal Visual Question Answering (VQA) systems for healthcare applications.
The study uses GI endoscopy cases to evaluate nine existing systems, highlighting the gap between strong benchmark performance and faithful clinical reasoning.
While parameter-efficient adaptation improves challenge performance, it doesn't guarantee that the AI's answers are complete or clinically sound.

stories.title: TikStance: A Multimodal and Hierarchical Dataset for Multi-target Stance Analysis in TikTok Political Conversations
stories.author: Bowen Zhang
bullet_points: Introduces TikStance, a novel multimodal and hierarchical dataset specifically designed for stance detection.
Addresses the challenge of analyzing political discourse on short-video platforms like TikTok, which lacks suitable datasets.
The dataset comprises 161 videos and 13,876 comments covering political discussions related to the 2024 U.S. election.

stories.title: In-Place Tokenizer Expansion for Pre-trained LLMs
stories.author: Mathias Lechner
bullet_points: Current LLM tokenizers are fixed based on initial pre-training corpus priorities.
Adding new languages later can lead to inefficient tokenization (more tokens per word), increasing latency and resource use.
The impact of this inefficiency is more critical for compact models compared to large cloud models.

stories.title: Expanding the Lexicon of Ge'ez Based African Languages: A Comparative Study of Amharic and Tigrinya
stories.author: Wolfgang Nejdl
bullet_points: Addresses the performance degradation of Multilingual Pre-trained Language Models (PLMs) on low-resource, non-Latin-script African languages due to tokenizer limitations.
Introduces VEXMLM, a vocabulary-extended variant of XLM-R specifically designed for the Ge'ez-script languages, Amharic and Tigrinya.
Evaluates the proposed model across 19 African languages, aiming to improve NLP capabilities for underrepresented linguistic communities.

stories.title: Mask-Aware Policy Gradients for Diffusion Language Models
stories.author: Philipp Krähenbühl
bullet_points: The research addresses the challenge of applying Reinforcement Learning (RL) to Masked Diffusion Language Models (MDLMs).
A key hurdle is the intractability of log-likelihood estimation in MDLMs, which existing methods approximate poorly.
The proposed method introduces 'Mask-Aware Policy Gradients' to account for the sequential decision-making process during MDLM generation.

stories.title: EEG shows brain can simultaneous encode two speech streams
stories.author: giuliomagnifico
bullet_points: EEG technology demonstrated the brain's capacity to simultaneously process two distinct speech streams.
This suggests advanced capabilities in auditory processing and cognitive multitasking.
The finding has implications for neuroscience, human-computer interaction, and potential assistive technologies.

stories.title: Linus Torvalds on LLM usage in kernel development
stories.author: lore.kernel.org via thang
bullet_points: Linus Torvalds, a key figure in Linux kernel development, has commented on the use of Large Language Models (LLMs).
The discussion touches upon the integration and potential impact of AI tools within the highly technical domain of kernel development.
This represents a moderate but significant discussion point regarding the future tooling and development practices in core open-source infrastructure.

stories.title: I Let an AI Agent Run My Cloud Ops for a Week: Here's What Broke
stories.author: muskan_bandta
bullet_points: First-hand experiment testing AI agent autonomy in real-world cloud operations.
Analyzes the successes and critical failures of AIOps in production environments.
Raises questions about the current readiness of AI for critical, on-call infrastructure management.
